findings.title: Date-override check allows slots that only partially overlap the override
findings.body: The condition marks a slot as outside an override only when slotEndTime is before or the same as the override start, or slotStartTime is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, starts inside and ends after it, or starts exactly at the override end is treated as inside the override and allowed. Since fixed-host slots are generated from aggregate availability, this lets a round-robin event be booked while the fixed host is unavailable.

findings.title: Fixed host with no working hours on a day is treated as available
findings.body: This `workingHours.find(...)` only rejects a slot when a working-hour entry for the day exists and the slot start is outside that entry. If no entry has `days` including `slotStartTime.day()`, `find` returns undefined and execution continues to the busy check, which can return true. For a round-robin slot generated by another host on a day the fixed host does not work, this makes the fixed host appear available and allows a booking outside their schedule.

findings.title: Working-hours check ignores slot end time/event length
findings.body: `end` is assigned the same value as `start`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` only checks whether `slotStartTime` is after the working hour end. It never validates that `slotStartTime + eventLength` fits within the working hours. A slot starting inside a fixed host's working hours but ending after them will be accepted, again undermining the fixed-host availability check.

findings.title: Multiple same-day date overrides are not all considered
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find` returns true as soon as one matching-day override is outside the slot, causing `checkIfIsAvailable` to return false immediately. Later same-day overrides that do contain the slot are never checked. If a fixed host has several overrides on one day, for example 10-11 and 14-15, a slot inside the later override can be blocked because the first override did not encompass it.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with strict equality
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares object references, not timestamps, so it is always false. This branch was presumably meant to identify equal start/end overrides with `isSame`. As written, that case falls through and can produce the wrong availability result.

findings.title: Round-robin fixed-host date override scenario is not tested
findings.body: The PR title/description says date overrides of fixed hosts should be taken into account for round-robin events, but the added test only covers a personal event date override with a different invitee timezone. The new `checkIfIsAvailable` date-override and working-hours paths for fixed hosts are the most complex part of this change and have no regression test.
